reply.thought: I need to determine each customer's net balance by retrieving their orders and calculating order amounts minus refunds, but I must use the net_balance tool for each customer instead of doing arithmetic myself.
The customer ID CUST001 doesn't exist, so I need to find which customers are in the batch by listing orders and identifying the customers involved in the refunds.

I have the list of orders with customers and amounts. The refunds are for customers cobalt (order 272, 8656¢), birch (order 274, 1382¢), and cobalt again (order 275, 2304¢). I need to compute each customer’ net balance (total order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance for each customer.
I have Acme’s net balance. Next I need the net balance for Birch, whose orders are 271 (29142¢) and 274 (20980¢) with a refund of 1382¢ on 274.
I have Birch’ net balance. Next I need the net balance for Cobalt, whose orders are 272 (21885¢) and 275 (13448¢) with refunds of 8656¢ on 272 and 2304¢ on 275.
I now have all customers’ net balances: Acme 62169¢, Birch 50122¢, Cobalt 35333¢. I will record a payout for each customer using record_payout.
Recorded payout for Acme. Next I need to record payouts for Birch and Cobalt.
Recorded payout for Birch. Next I need to record the payout for Cobalt.

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_cent'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: The tool expects the argument name 'amount_cents' (with an 's'), not 'amount_cent'. I need to correct the spelling and call record_payout again for Cobalt.
All payouts have been recorded successfully. I will now finish the batch with the required report.
